title: QBR / Health Check - Seabreeze Retail
summary: Quarterly review focused on usage growth (35% q/q), unexpected cost drivers around chat endpoints, two small reliability incidents in November traced to a network flake on a private VPC region. Redwood recommended batching/quantization adjustments and a pilot on Dedicated capacity for peak workloads. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send updated usage breakdown, pricing for Dedicated commitment tiers, and SOC2 / security pack; Seabreeze to share pinpointed prompt set and schedule benchmark week of 2025-12-15.
next_steps: Redwood: Send detailed usage-by-route CSV and per-token cost breakdown (due: 2025-12-05)
Redwood: Share Dedicated capacity pricing and three-month pilot proposal (due: 2025-12-08)
Seabreeze: Provide representative prompt set and sample traffic patterns for benchmark (due: 2025-12-10)
All: Schedule benchmark/validation week for 2025-12-15 to 2025-12-19
action_items: Lina Park: Compile per-route usage and anomalous spike analysis, attach screenshot of Console latency chart (due: 2025-12-05)
Marco Rivas: Prepare Dedicated pilot config and expected throughput numbers for their traffic profile (due: 2025-12-08)
Aisha Khan: Share top-50 prompts and labels for quality checks; note data residency requirements (due: 2025-12-10)
Priya Suresh: Provide access logs snippet and VPC config for the Nov 18 incident (due: 2025-12-07)
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-12-03
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Lina Park (Redwood AE), Marco Rivas (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Head of ML, Seabreeze), Tom Delgado (VP Eng, Seabreeze), Priya Suresh (Platform Eng, Seabreeze)

Summary (auto): QBR covering usage, cost, reliability. Discussed Dedicated vs hosted for peak traffic, batching and quantization recommendations, security checklist. Agreed benchmark week and follow-up artifacts.

[00:00] Lina Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, we have Lina and Marco from Redwood.
[00:06] Aisha Khan: Hi yeah, hi, Aisha here.
[00:08] Tom Delgado: Tom here.
[00:09] Priya Suresh: Priya on my end.
[00:12] Lina Park: Great, we'll jump right in - Marco will take us through the reliability and infra notes and then we'll look at usage and cost.
[00:22] Marco Rivas: Thanks, Lina. Quick note up front: overall 99.95% availability for November, two customer-facing incidents - both short. One on Nov 8 was a transient network issue in eu-west private region, second on Nov 18 was a routing flake during our autoscale event. Both are recorded in the incident log, root cause is a network policy propagation delay - we rolled a fix.
[00:48] Priya Suresh: Can you share the incident IDs? Our infra team saw a spike in 502s around 11/18 and we'd like to correlate.
[00:56] Marco Rivas: Yep, incident IDs, I'll include them in the follow-up. Also note, the 502s were fronted by your VPC peering - so the logs show the latency between their NAT and the Redwood edge. There was a mis-synced route table.
[01:15] Aisha Khan: That matches what we saw. The spike lasted maybe 6 minutes, but it impacted a small set of checkout flows, so it was visible in SLOs. Not a full outage but acceptable hit to error budget.
[01:30] Lina Park: Thanks for confirming. On usage - nice growth, 35% quarter over quarter across chat and embeddings. Biggest driver is the new recommendation microflow hitting chat endpoints more frequently. We noticed cost per chat token is trending up because of unbatched small requests.
[01:52] Tom Delgado: Yeah, those recommendation calls are short, like 40-120 tokens, but they're very high QPS. We're seeing a lot of single-message calls, so batching could help. Marco, what are the options?
[02:05] Marco Rivas: For short, high-QPS calls we usually recommend two levers: client-side batching or Redwood's server-side batching window tune. There's also prefix caching / KV cache for repeated preambles - though that helps when prompts share a common prefix. For recommendation microflows, batching + a smaller model quantized profile often gives the best unit-economics.
[02:28] Aisha Khan: When you say quantized profile, are you referring to the 4-bit profiles you mentioned last quarter? How does that affect quality?
[02:36] Marco Rivas: Right - our 4-bit quantized variants reduce token compute cost by ~35-50% depending on model. For many classification and recommendation tasks, quality drop is minimal; for open-ended chat it needs evals. We'll run quality gates on your prompt set.
[02:52] Priya Suresh: We've been hesitant to use dedicated because of procurement time and also our data residency constraints. But cost for peak days is high and capacity sometimes throttles.
[03:05] Lina Park: Totally understandable. Dedicated offers predictable throughput and isolation, which can stop throttling in peak windows. We can propose a short pilot - 4 weeks - on a small Dedicated pool sized for their 99th percentile peak. That lets you validate performance and SLOs without big procurement.
[03:25] Tom Delgado: Procurement is always the drag though. Is there a bridge approach - like reserved host blocks plus hosted overflow?
[03:33] Marco Rivas: Yes, that's a common pattern. We call it reserved + burst: commit to a baseline Dedicated pool, and traffic above that is served by hosted instances with policy-based routing. That keeps costs down and provides fallback.
[03:47] Aisha Khan: Can you give us expected cost delta for that pattern? We're looking at a 20-30% reduction on days where batching is effective but worried about baseline commit cost.
[03:58] Lina Park: We'll send a model-specific cost projection. For your traffic profile - given your short messages and high QPS - combining batching, 4-bit quantization, and a small Dedicated baseline typically drops unit cost by ~25% in our case studies. We'll attach the spreadsheet.
[04:17] Priya Suresh: On security: last Q we asked about KMS integration and audit logs. Has there been any change? We need HSM/KMS for keys and 13 month audit trace retention.
[04:29] Marco Rivas: KMS integrations are available for Private and Dedicated; hosted can use Redwood-managed keys with customer KMS available for Enterprise tiers. Audit logs retention is configurable - we can do 13 months for Enterprise customers. I'll include SOC 2 and our security pack in the follow-up.
[04:45] Aisha Khan: Great. Also, does Dedicated support customer KMS in the EU region? That's critical because of GDPR controls.
[04:53] Marco Rivas: Yes, Dedicated in eu-west supports customer-managed keys via your KMS. We'll confirm the exact region mapping in the doc.
[05:02] Tom Delgado: Back on reliability - what are the recommended SLOs we should set? We lost a bit of trust after the 11/18 flake.
[05:10] Lina Park: We typically recommend a latency SLO (p95) and an availability SLO. For your checkout flows p95 < 300ms is reasonable; availability > 99.9% for the Dedicated pilot. We'll help define SLA targets for the pilot period.
[05:28] Priya Suresh: Can we add tracing headers so we can correlate request IDs across our systems and Redwood? We want to map front-end to model latency.
[05:36] Marco Rivas: Absolutely. We support trace ID passthrough and can add extra metadata. There's a header-based solution and we'll send a short snippet for your engineering team.
[05:47] Aisha Khan: About quality monitoring - we want regression alerts tied to prompt sets. You mentioned eval hooks?
[05:55] Marco Rivas: Yes, Redwood Optimize supports prompt-set driven quality checks and automatic regression alerts. You can upload golden outputs and we run periodic evals; we'll triage failing prompts. Good fit for recommendation reranking.
[06:08] Tom Delgado: Who from Redwood will run the benchmark? We want someone to be on standby during the week.
[06:13] Lina Park: Marco will lead the benchmark validation with support from our Solutions Engineer team. We'll assign a dedicated point who can be in the run channel.
[06:22] Marco Rivas: I'll do the bench lead and provide the test harness and expected metrics table.
[06:28] Aisha Khan: For the pilot, what telemetry should we share? We can give logs, traces, and a synthetic load generator. Anything else?
[06:37] Marco Rivas: The prompt set, QPS distribution, percentiles for token length, and a few quality examples. Also your throughput target for 99th percentile.
[06:46] Priya Suresh: One more item: we've seen memory pressure on our side when clients kept open SSE streams during high traffic. Any recommendation?
[06:54] Marco Rivas: For streaming we recommend short-lived streams and keep-alives tuned; we also provide server-side throttles and backpressure signals. We'll include stream tuning recommendations.
[07:05] Aisha Khan: Ok good - let's talk timeline. Lina?
[07:09] Lina Park: Proposed timeline: send artifacts and pricing by 12/08, Seabreeze shares prompt set by 12/10, pilot run 12/15-12/19, follow-up QBR/end of pilot review 12/22. Does that work?
[07:22] Tom Delgado: Sounds fine, procurement will try to expedite the small commit.
[07:26] Priya Suresh: We'll try to have the prompt set and logs by the 10th.
[07:30] Aisha Khan: One last question: in the November cost spike, was there any unusual model choice?
[07:36] Marco Rivas: Quick look shows a small shift to a higher-capacity model in a canary - likely a team test. We'll point to the commit in the usage CSV.
[07:45] Aisha Khan: Ok, please highlight that.
[07:48] Marco Rivas: Will do.
[08:00] (silence, shared screen)
[10:22] Tom Delgado: Are we able to get the console widget that shows token-level cost per route? Our finance team wants that for invoicing.
[10:31] Lina Park: Yes, we can export per-route cost CSV and set up a permissions view for finance. We'll include example export and permission steps.
[12:05] Priya Suresh: On the audit side, can you confirm whether you store logs in a customer-managed S3?
[12:12] Marco Rivas: For Dedicated and Private, yes you can configure outbound to your S3. For hosted customers we provide log ingestion options and can set up a push to your bucket on request for Enterprise.
[14:00] Aisha Khan: Any blockers we should be aware of?
[14:06] Lina Park: Biggest blocker is procurement lead time for Dedicated and getting the representative prompt set. Otherwise it's operational tuning which we can help with.
[14:18] Tom Delgado: Ok, procurement will try to get the PO for the small baseline.
[14:22] Aisha Khan: And security - we'll want the SOC2 docs and the KMS region mapping.
[14:27] Marco Rivas: We'll attach SOC2 and KMS details.
[14:33] Lina Park: Great. Quick recap of action items: Marco will send incident IDs and bench harness; Lina will send usage CSV and pricing spreadsheet; Aisha and Priya will share prompts and logs.
[14:46] Aisha Khan: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[14:49] Tom Delgado: Thanks.
[14:50] Priya Suresh: Thanks all.
[14:53] Lina Park: We'll follow up by Friday with the artifacts.
[44:30] End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker labels may be approximate; occasional transcription errors (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache, "Redwood dedicate"), and timestamps are sampled.
